spans.text: Celestial beasts that reside primarily within the Heavens, but sometimes wander out into the Material Plane. They can mostly be found in the Valley of Setting Dreams, where they live among its residents. These inviting, peaceful creatures are the final state of souls that seek eternal peace and wish to break free from the cycle of death and rebirth. Finding satisfaction in their eternal existence, mortal souls passing on from a cycle of life become such a creature. If an icon is ever destroyed, its spirit re-enters the cycle of death and rebirth, and should that soul ever complete its mortal life again it will likely resume the same shape and form as the icon it once was.

Icons mostly resemble wild animals such as birds, lions, deer, elephants, etc., but some rare and powerful ones can have unique forms or resemble beasts such as dragons or greater mythological animals. Icons can form in any plane where souls find eternal peace, any their appearance.

Icons quietly protect and observe the planes they live in. When they sense danger or see a threat to their domain, they alert a celestial overseer such as an archon, deva, or other divine representative so that the realm’s authorities can be prepared. In rare situations they will fight, but only to protect the pure and good, or those closest to them.

Icons can speak to others through telepathic communication, but they do not do so using words. They relay concepts and emotions to those they speak to, giving them a perspective or message as if the creature had come to it themselves. The creature they speak to this way can feel the emotion behind the icon, fully comprehending its perception of whatever it is trying to convey. To this end, an icon expressing gratitude, love or trust to another also gives the gift of allowing that creature to share in those emotions, and so communication with icons is often a pleasant experience. Consequently, wronging one results in it sharing its grief, sadness or disdain. Any who attempts to hunt or harm an icon finds themselves sharing in the icon’s terror, anger, or panic, and become emotionally disoriented.

Icons can appear in any plane, not just the Heavens or the upper planes. Creatures that find genuine peace in the chaotic conditions of more devastating or hellish places can also become icons, though these are often more indicative of the plane in which they were born. Those born in the Heavens, for example, feature a soft golden glow, angelic colors and appearances, and are soft and inviting. Those born in the Beastlands, however, might have wild colorations and seem more like creatures of the hunt, resembling mythological beasts more often than not. Finally, those born of more mechanical planes may be more construct-like or feature mechanical elements on their body, seeming as augmented as their fellows.

When a plane is the natural anchoring point of a type of fiend, it is more likely that a creature meeting the conditions to become an icon will become that type of fiend instead. The same is true of souls in the abyss becoming demons. Within Somnus Domina’s most ancient and divine schools of thought, it is proposed that icons are a counterpart to yokai, representing the manifestation of positive and peaceful emotions given shape.
